Title: Safety and Loss Control Director
Description: 7.4.6SAFETY and LOSS CONTROLBranch Safety SuperintendentJOB DESCRIPTIONJob Summary: Under the direction of the Corporate Safety Director, the Branch Safety Superintendent effectively implements company safety programs, practices, and procedures to reduce the frequency and severity of accidental loss in the areas of worker’s compensation, general and auto liability, and property; ensures company compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, which are designed to protect the human, financial, and physical assets of the company; creates a branch-wide safety culture through safety training, risk assessments, and behavior modification programs.CHARACTERISTIC JOB TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES May include any and/or all of the following:The Branch Safety Superintendent(s) will be members of the Safety Committee.  They will be responsible to report to the committee of the current safety situations, concerns, and progress as it pertains the branch safety.Assist in developing programs to ensure the companies compliance with federal, state, and local safety-related regulations, in addition to other environmental health, safety, and loss prevention standards and guidelines.Perform required Safety Inspections and Safety Audits. Conducts claims investigations and evaluates risk management claims information to identify significant hazards and loss trends; identifies and recommends preventive measures and corrective actions. Performs regular physical inspections of company projects, equipment, and operations; identifies hazards and incidents of regulatory non-compliance and recommends corrective measures. Provides ongoing safety and loss prevention training to various company personnel to reduce the frequency and severity of accidental losses. Provide one-on-one performance reviews with Safety Coordinators within the branch.Administer disciplinary action in strict accordance with the GSL disciplinary policy for all branch safety infractions.KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES AND PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICSKnowledge of federal, state, and local loss prevention regulations Verbal and written communication skills Interpersonal/human relations skills Planning/organizational skills Ability to implement, and control our safety program Ability to conduct safety inspections of company projects and equipment MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Education and experience equivalent to:Three (3) years of related experience. The Safety Superintendent must have a good working knowledge of the electrical trade and established safe electrical work procedures.Safety DirectorJOB DESCRIPTIONFlag this photoThe Safety Director is the Company’s primary Loss Control Officer. He/She oversees the development, training, implementation of the Loss Control program.  This includes (but is not limited to) the practices, policies, and procedures intended to reduce the frequency and severity of accidental loss in the areas of worker’s compensation, general and auto liability, and property; ensures company compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, which are designed to protect the human, financial, and physical assets of the company; develops and promotes a company-wide safety culture through safety training, risk assessments, and behavior modification programs.Safety Director will work closely with operations to insure all concerns are being addressed in accordance with the written Loss Control Program in addition to all other Company Policies and Procedures.  The Safety Director reports directly to the President and assumes all organizational accountability for the three phases of the Loss Control Program:Development and TrainingAccident Prevention and ImplementationCase ManagementDevelopment and Training of the GSL Loss Control Program (Safety Program Manager): His/her responsibilities include supervising and all aspect of insurance filings and claims as well as ensuring safety in the workplace. This will be accomplished by developing, coordinating, administering and implementing comprehensive training programs in occupational, industrial and environmental safety. The Safety Director (and the Safety Program Manager) must have strong administrative skills and are responsible to:Be knowledgeable of the continuous changes, trends, and hazards related to the industry. The U.S. Department of Labor describes the position as one "with a rapid change in skill set requiring new knowledge."Be required to develop and update the GSL Loss Control Program to ensure the companies compliance with Case Management federal, state, and local safety-related regulations, in addition to other environmental health, safety, and loss prevention standards and guidelines. Develop, implement and maintain quality employee training programs; Be responsible for the quality and timeliness of required training.Establish and maintain complete safety and training records. Is required to maintain up-to date records on all approved vendors and sub-contractors to they meet the minimum requirements as stated in the Loss Control Program.Accident Prevention / Implementation of the GSL Loss Control Program (Branch Safety Superintendent): The Safety Director will directly supervise the Branch Safety Superintendent(s) (if applicable).  The Safety Director is accountable to insure that all employees are effectively implementing company safety programs, practices, and procedures to reduce the frequency and severity of accidental loss.  His/Her duties also include developing and promoting a safety culture through safety training, risk assessments, and behavior modification programs. The Safety Director and/or delegated Accident Prevention / Implementation personnel must have strong leadership skills and will be responsible to: Conduct safety audits and inspections to ensure compliance with occupational and environmental health and safety requirements as defined in the GSL Loss Control Program. Performs regular physical inspections of company projects, equipment, and operations; identifies hazards and incidents of regulatory non-compliance and recommends corrective measures.Provide ongoing safety and loss prevention training to various company personnel to reduce the frequency and severity of accidental losses. Provide one-on-one performance reviews with all active Project Safety Coordinators.Administer or review all disciplinary action in strict accordance with the GSL disciplinary policy for all safety infractions.Case Management:In addition to the requirements and demands needed to develop and implement the Loss Control Program, the Safety Director must commit the necessary focus, time and resources to effectively manage all loss control cases.The Safety Director is ultimately responsible to manage work related injury claims to minimize exposure to the company, including all General Liability, Worker’s Compensation, and Auto Insurance filings and claims. The Safety Director will respond to reported accidents to evaluate current best practices and recommend changes where necessary. The Safety Director is responsible to manage all reported cases resulting in theft and/or vandalism.Conduct or review claims investigations and evaluates risk management claims information to identify significant hazards and loss trends; identifies and recommends preventive measures and corrective actions. The Safety Director will be required to be well versed and current with all aspects of the Safety Programs and will be required to:Chair the Safety Committee. Participate as member of the Executive Committee.Evaluate and report all safety statistics, concerns, and recommendations to the Executive Committee. Educational and Experience RequirementsIt is preferable that Safety Director to have a degree in Safety Management, Safety Engineering, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Environment Health and Safety, or a related field.  However, extensive experience and knowledge of environmental and occupational health and safety, along with an established track record of success, will be considered as a substitute for the educational requirements.  The Safety Director must have a good working knowledge of the electrical trade and established safe electrical work procedures.  The Safety Director must have the following skills:Verbal and written communication skills Interpersonal/human relations skills Planning/organizational skills Adequate computer skills, including a proficiency in using common word processing software, spreadsheet software, database applications, project and presentation software, and email.
